text:
alex: Heads up — eu-west GPU capacity hit 100% around 09:11 UTC, new inference jobs queued, autoscaler didn't provision new gpu-ws-* nodes. Seeing API 429s from hosted endpoints.

marta: on it, checking autoscaler metrics and cloud provider events. received CA alerts but no scale-up events?

ops-bot: [ALERT] cluster-autoscaler: scale-up failed: no matching instance types available in eu-west-1 for gpu-accelerator=rtx6000 (requested 4 nodes) (event_ts=2024-11-03T09:12:02Z)

sandeep: pinging cloud quota/spot-supply — looks like spot pool in eu-west reported low capacity at 09:10, fallback to on-demand was disabled for this nodepool (config: allowFallback=false).

jess: oh — that nodepool was created last month for cheaper training bursts. We left fallback off to control spend.

ryan: quick mitigation: can we toggle allowFallback=true on the autoscaler/nodegroup to let on-demand spin up while we investigate spot supply?

marta: trying to flip allowFallback for nodepool gpu-spot-eu. applying change now.

alex: also seeing a weird heartbeat gap from the cluster-autoscaler leader elect — CA logs show repeated leader-election timeouts around 09:09-09:11. might be related.

ops-bot: [CA LOG] E1103 09:10:57.123 scale_up.go:341] failed to scale up: Retryable error: leader election lost, skipping scale-up

aline: if the leader lost lock, CA won't process scale decisions. Is kube-apiserver latency spiking?

marta: apiserver latency normal (<200ms) but etcd ops spiked for a few seconds at 09:08, logs show compaction window and disk iops borderline. engineering tracked a noisy backup job in the control plane earlier.

sandeep: allowFallback toggle applied, provisioning on-demand requesting nodes now: "Requesting 2 x on-demand rtx6000"

ops-bot: [CLOUD] provision request submitted: req-0a1b2c (status: pending)

jess: while nodes come up, can we evict best-effort/low-priority batch jobs from GPU pool to free slots for hosted inference? Suggest tainting gpu-spot-eu with dedicated-inference=true:NoSchedule then cordon low-priority nodes.

ryan: agreed — I can run a dry-run eviction list: kubectl get pods -n training -o jsonpath='{range .items[?(@.spec.priorityClassName=="best-effort")]}{.metadata.name}
'{end}' | head -n 30

marta: executed taint and started targeted evictions for pods with priorityClass=best-effort. freed 6 GPUs so far. Hosted traffic drop from 429 -> 503 -> 200 quickly.

alex: provisioning request succeeded, new on-demand nodes joined at 09:25 UTC, cluster capacity back to 95%. Need follow-ups: leader election flapping + backup job compaction timing causing brief CA outage.

aline: recommend immediate post-incident steps: 1) revert allowFallback to original policy after we confirm spot supply; 2) gate backups during peak control plane windows; 3) add a CA healthcheck and alert for leader-election loss (different noise threshold).

sandeep: cost note — using on-demand fallback for ~15m added ~$1.8k estimated to this incident (training jobs kept running previously). tagging the incident with cost-impact.

jess: I'll open a runbook PR to include emergency taint/evict steps and a synthetic health check for leader-election lost.

marta: creating incident ticket with timeline + logs, will add action items and assign owners.

alex: thanks team. moving to follow-up channel for root cause and postmortem.

ops-bot: [INCIDENT] incident-2156789012 created, severity=P2, owner=marta, start_ts=2156789012

ryan: small note — consider a short-term quota reservation in eu-west for dedicated inference pool so we have guaranteed baseline if spot supply drops.

sandeep: noted, I'll draft a proposal for reserved capacity vs cost thresholds.

marta: last check: all hosted endpoints returned to nominal. closing incident channel in 30m unless anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
